main_text.p: re potuerit, noluit Deus, ut primùm ictum ab illo noctur-no grassatore exspectaremus, verùm si eum præveniendo occidamus, impune nos hoc facturos, ac laturos, edixit. Et solent Theologi ad illum scri-pturæ locum eandem ratio-nem exprimere, quam juris-consulti tradiderunt. Scilicet quod merito ignoret paterfa-milias, num veniat fur noctur-nus occidendi animo, num vero furandi. Quasi dicant, justum armorum metum, ac tenorem non vanum vulneris vel cædis, etiam justam causam esse, cur adversarium interficiamus.

Confirmatur hoc 2. Effato illo Paulino. Ephes c. 5. v.29. Nemo unquam odio habuit propriam carnem, verum eam fovet, atque nu-trit. Ast qui primùm ictum ex-spectat & periculo se subjicit mutilationis membrorum ac

page.notes: The catchword "vitæ," is the first word of the next page and is kept out of the text. The mark in the left margin beside "solent" is a printed spot or bullet with no note text; it is not transcribed. The marginal note "Ephes c. 5. v.29." is set in small type; the initial letter reads as "Ephef" in the scan, rendered here as "Ephes" under the long-s rule. The word "solent" is read from the scan, the initial letter partly hidden by the mark.
